mainTopic: The עין הרע and זרע יוסף, and how ארץ ישראל was divided: the portions of the מרגלים, the מתלוננים, עדת קרח and בנות צלפחד
overview: This amud finishes the story of בני יוסף, who tell יהושע they do not need to fear the עין הרע. Two sources are brought for this: רבי אבהו reads 'עלי עין' as 'עולי עין', and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא compares יוסף's descendants to fish hidden under water. The גמרא then goes back to the ברייתא about how ארץ ישראל was divided. עולא proves from the word 'חיו' that יהושע and כלב took the portions of the מרגלים. Two ברייתות disagree about whether the מתלוננים and עדת קרח had portions, and the גמרא explains that they disagree about a היקש comparing the מתלוננים to the מרגלים. רב פפא then asks אביי a series of questions. He asks how the ten portions of מנשה add up under each view of who the land was divided among, and the גמרא answers that בנות צלפחד inherited from uncles the פסוק does not name. The amud ends with רב פפא asking what the פסוק is actually counting when it lists those ten portions.

steps.title: יוסף's descendants say the evil eye cannot harm them
steps.stepSummary: בני יוסף answer יהושע that the עין הרע has no power over them, based on רבי אבהו's reading of a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We come from the family of יוסף, and the evil eye has no power over that family. The פסוק says, 'יוסף is a fruitful son, a fruitful son by a spring (עלי עין).' רבי אבהו said: Don't read it as 'עלי עין' (by a spring). Read it as 'עולי עין' (rising above the eye).
steps.whatsHappening: בני יוסף reply to יהושע's warning about the עין הרע. They say they do not need to worry, because יוסף's family is protected from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עין can mean a spring or an eye. רבי אבהו reads the פסוק so that יוסף is 'above the eye,' meaning the עין הרע cannot reach him. בני יוסף use this to show that his descendants share the same protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Seed, meaning descendants
The evil eye (עין הרע)
Has power or control over
Don't read it this way; read it another way (a way of drawing a lesson from a word's sound)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the פסוק is spelled differently. It is a way of drawing an extra lesson from a similar-sounding word, while the text itself stays the same.

phrases.english: They said to him: We are from the seed of Yosef,
phrases.notes: 'They' are בני יוסף, answering יהושע's advice about the evil eye from just before this.

phrases.english: over whom the evil eye has no power,
as it is written: "Yosef is a fruitful son,
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:22

phrases.english: a fruitful son by a spring,"
and Rabbi Abbahu said:
Do not read it as "alei ayin" (by a spring),
but rather as "olei ayin" (rising above the eye).
phrases.notes: The word עין means both 'spring' and 'eye,' so the pun works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from before this section, where יהושע warned בני יוסף about the עין הרע.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יוסף's descendants are above the עין הרע, as shown by reading עלי עין as עולי עין.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the עין הרע cannot harm זרע יוסף
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 49:22 as read by רבי אבהו

steps.title: A second source: יוסף's descendants are like fish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns the same idea from 'ויִדגו,' which compares יוסף's descendants to fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said the source is this פסוק: 'May they multiply like fish (ויִדגו) in the midst of the land.' Water covers the fish in the sea, so the eye cannot rule over them. In the same way, the eye cannot rule over the descendants of יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: A different אמורא gives another פסוק to prove the same point: the עין הרע cannot harm יוסף's descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ויִדגו sounds like דָּג, a fish. Fish are hidden under water, so no one's eye can see them and harm them. The ברכה compares יוסף's descendants to fish, so they are protected the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, meaning from this source
And may they multiply, a word related to דָּג (fish)
Fish

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources that the עין הרע has no power over זרע יוסף: רבי אבהו learns it from 'עולי עין,' and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns it from 'ויִדגו,' like fish hidden under water.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: from here:
"And may they multiply like fish in the midst of the land";
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:16. יעקב is blessing אפרים and מנשה, and ויִדגו sounds like דָּג, 'fish.'

phrases.english: just as fish in the sea
have water covering them
and the eye has no power over them,
so too the seed of Yosef:
the eye has no power over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אֲמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same idea as רבי אבהו in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the עין הרע cannot harm זרע יוסף

steps.title: The ברייתא: יהושע and כלב took the spies' portions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: יהושע and כלב took the portions of the מרגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The spies: יהושע and כלב took their portions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא about dividing ארץ ישראל and quotes its next ruling. This sets up the question of where the ruling comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten מרגלים who died were each supposed to get a share in the land. The ברייתא rules that their shares went to יהושע and כלב, the two faithful spies, instead of to the spies' own families.

keyTerms.meaning: The spies sent by משה to scout ארץ ישראל
Took their portion

phrases.english: The spies: Yehoshua and Kalev
took their portion.
phrases.notes: 'Their portion' means the spies' shares of the land, not just יהושע and כלב's own shares.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of בני יוסף and goes back to analyzing the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The portions in ארץ ישראל of the dead מרגלים went to יהושע and כלב.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק teaches that יהושע and כלב took the spies' portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ruling it just quoted. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is not obvious, since you might expect the spies' shares to go to their own children. So the גמרא wants a פסוק that supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words learned? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק shows that יהושע and כלב took the spies' portions?

steps.title: עולא brings the verse 'they lived'
steps.stepSummary: עולא points to the פסוק saying that יהושע and כלב 'lived from those men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The פסוק says, 'And יהושע son of נון and כלב son of יפנה lived from those men.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by quoting a פסוק. Exactly what the פסוק means is explained in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'חיו,' 'lived,' together with 'from those men.' עולא will show that this phrase means more than simply surviving.

keyTerms.meaning: As the פסוק says
They lived

phrases.english: Ulla said: As the verse states:
"And Yehoshua son of Nun and Kalev son of Yefuneh
lived from those men"
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:38

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is במדבר 14:38, 'יהושע and כלב lived from those men.'

steps.title: 'Lived' cannot just mean they survived
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that 'חיו' cannot simply mean that they stayed alive, because another פסוק already says that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'lived' mean? If you say it means they literally stayed alive, a different פסוק already says this: 'Not one man of them was left except כלב son of יפנה and יהושע son of נון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'lived' means and rejects the simple reading. If it only meant they survived, it would repeat something another פסוק already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat itself for no reason. Since במדבר 26:65 already tells us that יהושע and כלב survived, 'חיו' in במדבר 14:38 must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (bringing up a possible reading in order to reject it)
Literally
Another פסוק

phrases.english: What is meant by "lived"?
If you say they literally lived,
but another verse is written:
"And not a man of them was left,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם כָּלֵב בֶּן יְפֻנֶּה וִיהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן״!
phrases.english: except Kalev son of Yefuneh and Yehoshua son of Nun"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 26:65

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״חָיוּ״? אִילֵּימָא חָיוּ מַמָּשׁ, וְהָא כְּתִיב קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests עולא's פסוק by rejecting the literal meaning of 'חיו.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Survival is already stated in במדבר 26:65, so reading it that way would make the word extra.

steps.title: 'Lived' means they lived in the spies' portions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'חיו' means יהושע and כלב lived on the spies' shares of the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'lived' mean? That they lived in their portion, meaning the portion of the spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of 'חיו.' This completes the source for the ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They lived from those men' now means they lived on what belonged to those men, the spies' land. This is exactly the ruling of step 3: יהושע and כלב took the spies' portions.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (bringing in the correct explanation)
In their portion

steps.whatToRemember: יהושע and כלב received the spies' portions. The source is 'חיו מן האנשים ההם,' which cannot simply mean survival, since that is already stated elsewhere.

phrases.english: Rather, what is meant by "lived"?
That they lived in their portion.
phrases.notes: 'Their portion' here means the portion of those men, the other spies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חיו' means they lived on the spies' portions of the land.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ruling of the ברייתא is supported by the פסוק: יהושע and כלב took the spies' portions.

steps.title: The ברייתא: the complainers and קרח's group had no portion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's next ruling: the מתלוננים and עדת קרח had no portion in the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The complainers and the group of קרח had no portion in the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the ברייתא. It is setting up a contradiction from a different ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the מרגלים, these groups were never given shares in ארץ ישראל at all. So there was nothing to pass on to anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The complainers who grumbled in the desert
The group of קרח, who rebelled against משה

phrases.english: The complainers and the group of Korach:
they had no portion in the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִתְלוֹנְנִין וַעֲדַת קֹרַח – לֹא הָיָה לָהֶן חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מתלוננים and עדת קרח were not given a portion in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says their portions went to יהושע and כלב
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא lists the מתלוננים and עדת קרח together with the מרגלים as groups whose portions יהושע and כלב took.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: The spies, the complainers and the group of קרח: יהושע and כלב took their portions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling of step 8 with a different ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יהושע and כלב took the portions of the מתלוננים and עדת קרח, those groups must have had portions to begin with. That contradicts the first ברייתא, which says they had none.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita: The spies,
the complainers and the group of Korach:
Yehoshua and Kalev took their portion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 8 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the מתלוננים and עדת קרח had no portion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says יהושע and כלב took their portions, which means they did have portions.

steps.title: The two ברייתות disagree about a היקש
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות reflect two תנאים who disagree about whether the מתלוננים are compared to the מרגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. One master compares the complainers to the spies, and one master does not compare the complainers to the spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One תנא learns through a היקש that the מתלוננים are like the מרגלים: they had portions, and those portions went to יהושע and כלב. The other תנא does not make this comparison, so in his view the מתלוננים never had a portion at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the contradiction can be explained
One master or Sage
Compares one case to another (makes a היקש)

steps.whatToRemember: All agree that the מרגלים' portions went to יהושע and כלב. Whether the מתלוננים also had portions that went to them depends on whether you compare them to the מרגלים.
steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות agree about the מרגלים. The disagreement is only about the מתלוננים, and it comes down to whether the היקש is made.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
one master compares the complainers to the spies,
and one master does not compare the complainers to the spies.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; מָר מַקֵּישׁ מִתְלוֹנְנִים לִמְרַגְּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources follow two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות give opposite facts about the מתלוננים.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree about whether the מתלוננים are compared to the מרגלים through a היקש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether the מתלוננים had a portion in the land depends on whether they are compared to the מרגלים.

steps.title: The ברייתא that lists the spies, the complainers and קרח's group together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the words of בנות צלפחד as naming three separate groups: the מרגלים, the מתלוננים, and עדת קרח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "Our father died in the wilderness" means צלפחד. "And he was not among the assembly" means the assembly of the spies. "That gathered themselves against ה'" means the complainers. "In the assembly of קרח" means just what it says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the תנא who puts the מתלוננים in the same group as the מרגלים. The ברייתא reads one פסוק as naming three different groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בנות צלפחד were explaining why their father still had a share in the land: he was not part of any group that lost its share. The ברייתא splits their words into three groups (spies, complainers, קרח's assembly). This shows that the complainers are listed side by side with the spies, as groups whose shares were lost.

keyTerms.meaning: The man from שבט מנשה who died in the desert and left only daughters
The group of spies who gave a bad report about the land
Those who gathered together against ה'
Just as it sounds, its plain meaning

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is explaining במדבר 27:3, the words of the daughters of צלפחד.

phrases.english: "Our father died in the wilderness": this is צלפחד.
"And he was not among the assembly":
this is the assembly of the spies.
"That gathered themselves together against ה'": these are the complainers.
"In the assembly of קרח": as it sounds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ברייתא from step 9, which grouped the מתלוננים with the מרגלים
steps.raayaObject: The view that the מתלוננים lost their share just like the מרגלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading במדבר 27:3 as naming three separate groups

steps.title: One Sage compares the complainers to the spies and the other does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the dispute: one תנא compares the מתלוננים to the מרגלים, and the other does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage compares the complainers to the spies, and one Sage does not compare the complainers to the spies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states plainly what the two ברייתות disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever compares the complainers to the spies holds that יהושע and כלב took the complainers' shares as well. Whoever does not compare them holds that the complainers' shares simply did not exist. So the two ברייתות do not contradict each other. They are two different views.

keyTerms.meaning: One Sage (literally 'master')
Compares one case to another, treating them the same way

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות disagree only about the complainers: should their lost shares be treated like the spies' shares, which went to יהושע and כלב?

phrases.english: One Sage compares the complainers to the spies,
and one Sage does not compare the complainers to the spies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the dispute behind the ברייתא just quoted
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two ברייתות reflect a real dispute about whether the מתלוננים are compared to the מרגלים

steps.title: Did יהושע and כלב take the entire land?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: if every complainer is like a spy, then יהושע and כלב would have inherited almost all of ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: According to the one who compares the complainers to the spies, did יהושע and כלב go and inherit all of ארץ ישראל?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the view that compares the מתלוננים to the מרגלים, because the result seems impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many Jews complained in the desert at one time or another. If all of them lost their shares to יהושע and כלב, those two would end up owning nearly the whole land. That cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Did they go and grab, did they press their claim
And they inherited

phrases.english: And רב פפא said to אביי:
And according to the one who compares the complainers to the spies,
did יהושע and כלב press their claim
and inherit all of ארץ ישראל?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וּלְמַאן דְּמַקֵּישׁ מִתְלוֹנְנִים לִמְרַגְּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks one side of the dispute just stated
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that compares the מתלוננים to the מרגלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: So many people complained that יהושע and כלב would inherit nearly the whole land, which is unreasonable

steps.title: Only the complainers in קרח's group
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that 'complainers' here means only the complainers who were part of קרח's group.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are talking about the complainers who were in the assembly of קרח.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא by narrowing who counts as 'complainers'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view that compares complainers to spies does not mean every Jew who ever complained. It means only the small group who complained together with קרח. So יהושע and כלב received only a limited number of extra shares.

keyTerms.meaning: The complainers who were part of קרח's group
We are saying, this is what we mean

phrases.english: He said to him:
We are talking about the complainers who were in the assembly of קרח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִתְלוֹנְנִים שֶׁבַּעֲדַת קֹרַח קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: defining which complainers are meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Complainers' means everyone who ever complained in the desert
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Complainers' means only those who complained along with קרח, a limited group

steps.title: The ten portions of מנשה fit the view that the land went to those who left מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא opens a new question. According to the view that the land was divided among those who left מצרים, the ten portions of מנשה make sense: six for the families and four for בנות צלפחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said to אביי: It works well according to the one who says the land was divided among those who left מצרים. That is what is written: "And ten portions fell to מנשה." Six for the six fathers' houses, and four for them. That makes ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up רב פפא's next challenge. First he shows how one view easily explains the ten portions of מנשה. The difficulty for the other view comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא ('it works well') signals the pattern: one view fits, and the other will be questioned. If the land went to those who left מצרים, then the count of ten works out. Six portions went to מנשה's six family groups, and four went to בנות צלפחד.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view), introducing a difficulty for the other view
Those who left מצרים
Portions, measured parcels of land
Fathers' houses, family groups within a שבט

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the full question yet. It only shows what works for one view. The challenge to the other view comes in step 16.

phrases.english: And רב פפא said to אביי:
It works well according to the one who says
that the land was divided among those who left מצרים,
that is what is written:
"And ten portions fell to מנשה":
phrases.notes: יהושע 17:5

phrases.english: six for the six fathers' houses,
phrases.notes: These are the six family groups of מנשה listed in יהושע 17:2.

phrases.english: and four of theirs: that makes ten.
phrases.notes: 'Theirs' means the daughters of צלפחד.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְיוֹצְאֵי מִצְרַיִם נִתְחַלְּקָה הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question from רב פפא about how the land was divided
steps.kashyaTarget: The opposing view about who the land was divided among (stated after this point)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The setup half: the ten portions of מנשה fit the view that the land went to those who left מצרים. The other view will be tested against this פסוק next.

steps.title: For the view of those who entered the land, there are only eight portions
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא completes his challenge. If the land went to those who entered ארץ ישראל, the count is six plus two, which is eight, not ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the land was divided among those who entered it, there were only eight portions: six for the six families, and two belonging to בנות צלפחד. That is eight!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא now makes the actual attack he set up in the previous step. Under the view of באי הארץ, the numbers add up to eight, but the פסוק speaks of ten portions for מנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view צלפחד himself gets no portion, because he did not enter the land. His daughters only receive what came through their grandfather חפר: a regular share plus צלפחד's firstborn share. That gives two, and two plus six is eight, so two portions are missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who entered ארץ ישראל
Eight
Fathers' houses, meaning family groups
Theirs, meaning belonging to בנות צלפחד

phrases.english: But according to the one who says it was divided among those who entered the land,
there were only eight portions:
six for the six fathers' houses,
and two that were theirs,
phrases.notes: These two come from their grandfather חפר: one regular share, plus the extra firstborn share since צלפחד was his firstborn.

phrases.english: that makes eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 15 set up by contrasting the two views.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that ארץ ישראל was divided among באי הארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this view the count comes to only eight portions, but the פסוק says מנשה received ten.

steps.title: The other view has the same problem, with only nine portions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around. Even the view of יוצאי מצרים reaches only nine portions, because the משנה says בנות צלפחד took three.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your own reasoning, even the one who says the land was divided among those who left מצרים gets only nine portions!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא. It argues that his question is not a special weakness of one view, because the other view also falls short of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says בנות צלפחד took three portions. Six family portions plus three equals nine, not ten. So the 'easy' view also needs an explanation, and the question cannot be used against just one side.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the question back on the asker
Those who left מצרים
Nine

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
even according to the one who says
the land was divided among those who left מצרים,
there are only nine!
phrases.notes: The משנה says בנות צלפחד took three portions. Six plus three is nine, so one is still missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 16 that only the באי הארץ view has a counting problem.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the miscount disproves only the באי הארץ view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The יוצאי מצרים view also falls short, reaching only nine, so the question applies to both views.

steps.title: They had uncles who are not mentioned in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: Both views fill the gap the same way. The יוצאי מצרים view adds one unmentioned uncle, and the באי הארץ view adds two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? They had one uncle on their father's side. So too here, say that they had two uncles on their father's side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer that fixes both views. בנות צלפחד received extra portions from uncles who died without children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other view must already say there was one hidden uncle in order to reach ten. Once that is accepted, the באי הארץ view can use the same idea with two uncles, which adds the two missing portions and brings eight up to ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must you say? Pointing to the answer you are forced to give
Father's brother, an uncle
So too, the same applies here

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
They had one uncle on their father's side;
phrases.notes: This is an uncle the פסוק never names, who died without children, so his share passed to their family.

phrases.english: so too here,
they had two uncles on their father's side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the counting problem raised in steps 16 and 17 for both views.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding unstated facts: unmentioned uncles whose shares passed to בנות צלפחד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The count should come only from the people the פסוק names, so the numbers do not reach ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were unmentioned uncles, one or two depending on the view, whose portions make up the full ten.

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the פסוק as giving them several inheritances
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads each phrase of the פסוק about בנות צלפחד as a separate inheritance: their father's, their grandfather's, and the firstborn share.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall surely give them' means their father's inheritance. 'Among their father's brothers' means their grandfather's inheritance. 'And you shall pass their father's inheritance to them' means the firstborn's portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the פסוק really gives בנות צלפחד more than one portion. This prepares the source for an uncle's portion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק becomes a separate share. They get their father's portion, a share in their grandfather חפר's estate, and the extra firstborn share that צלפחד was owed. This shows that the פסוק counts several distinct portions.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall surely give: a doubled verb
Their grandfather's inheritance
The firstborn's extra portion

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"You shall surely give them"
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:7

phrases.english: this is their father's inheritance.
"Among their father's brothers":
this is their grandfather's inheritance.
"And you shall pass their father's inheritance to them":
this is the firstborn's portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins bringing a source to support the uncles answer of step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That בנות צלפחד received several separate portions

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: they also took their uncle's portion
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns from the doubled words 'נתן תתן' that בנות צלפחד also took an uncle's portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: They also took the portion of their father's brother, as it says 'You shall surely give.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who gives the direct source for an uncle's portion. This supports the one-uncle answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled verb 'נתן תתן' seems extra, so he reads it as adding another portion, the share of an uncle. This gives a source in the פסוק for the uncle the גמרא needed in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of their father's brother
They took

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says:
they also took the portion of their father's brother,
as it says: "You shall surely give."
phrases.notes: 'Give' is said twice, and he reads the extra one as one more portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and gives the direct source for one uncle's portion.
steps.raayaObject: That בנות צלפחד inherited an uncle's portion
steps.raayaSupportSource: The doubled phrase נתן תתן in במדבר 27:7

steps.title: Where the second uncle comes from
steps.stepSummary: For the view that there were two uncles, the second uncle's portion is learned from the words 'אחזת נחלה' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says they had two uncles, that second portion is learned from the words 'a possession of an inheritance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: 'נתן תתן' gives only one uncle, so where does the second uncle come from? It finds a second extra phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אחזת נחלה' seem extra in the פסוק, so they teach one more portion. This gives the באי הארץ view a source for both missing portions and completes the count of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: A possession of an inheritance: words from the פסוק
It is derived, it comes out from

steps.whatToRemember: Both views reach ten portions for מנשה by saying בנות צלפחד inherited from uncles the פסוק does not name: one uncle for the יוצאי מצרים view, two for the באי הארץ view. Extra words in במדבר 27:7 are the source.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says
they had two uncles on their father's side,
that one is learned from "a possession of an inheritance."
phrases.notes: These words come from the same פסוק, במדבר 27:7: "נָתֹן תִּתֵּן לָהֶם אֲחֻזַּת נַחֲלָה."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר תְּרֵי אַחֵי דְּאַבָּא הֲוָה לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the source of step 20 so that it covers the two-uncle view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds an additional extra phrase in the פסוק to serve as the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only gives a source for one uncle, so the two-uncle view would have no source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words אחזת נחלה supply the source for the second uncle's portion.

steps.title: What is the verse counting when it lists the portions?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי what the פסוק is counting. Counting individual heirs would give far too many portions. Counting family houses would give only six. So why does the פסוק list the portions of בנות צלפחד separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said to אביי: What is the verse counting? If it is counting children, there were many! If it is counting fathers' houses, there were six!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא raises a new challenge to אביי about the פסוק that lists ten portions for the tribe of מנשה. Neither way of reading the count seems to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He sets up two options. If the פסוק counts everyone who inherited from a parent, like בנות צלפחד, there would be many more than ten portions. If it counts the main family houses, there are only six, and חפר is already one of them, so the separate portions of בנות צלפחד should not be counted at all.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse (here, the פסוק listing the portions of מנשה)
is counting, is listing
children, meaning people who inherited from their parents
fathers' houses, the main family branches
many, a lot

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about how many portions בנות צלפחד received. That was settled in the earlier steps. The question here is what kind of unit the פסוק uses when it counts.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
The verse, what is it counting?
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק that gives מנשה ten portions (יהושע 17:5).

phrases.english: If it is counting children,
phrases.notes: He means each person who inherited a share from a parent, the way בנות צלפחד did.

phrases.english: there were many!
If it is counting fathers' houses,
there were six!
phrases.notes: These are the six families listed in יהושע 17:2, and חפר is one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how בנות צלפחד received their portions, רב פפא raises a new difficulty about how the פסוק counts portions at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of ten portions for מנשה in the פסוק, which includes the portions of בנות צלפחד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: counting individual heirs would give far more than ten, and counting family houses would give only six. Neither reading explains listing בנות צלפחד's portions separately.
